name: Mint

companions.note: Mint's strong scent deters cabbage moths and aphids; keep in a container nearby rather than in the bed
Repels aphids and spider mites when grown nearby in containers

pnw_notes: Container planting is essential — mint spreads aggressively by underground runners and will take over a raised bed in one season. Four varieties in containers tucked between the raised beds: chocolate, lime, curly, and mojito mint. Cut back hard after flowering to prevent woodiness and encourage fresh growth. PNW summers suit mint well; consistent moisture is the main need. Dies back in winter and returns reliably in spring — container roots may need protection (move to a sheltered spot) if temps drop below 25°F.

frost_hardiness.notes: Dies back to the crown in winter and returns in spring. Container roots have less insulation than in-ground — move pots to a sheltered spot if sustained temps below 25°F are forecast.

planting_windows.notes: Spring plant into containers; establish before summer heat
Fall planting also works; roots establish well in cool temperatures
Harvest stems regularly to encourage bushy growth; peak flavor just before flowering in midsummer
